uncited: Hardware-Specific Optimization adapts volume rendering algorithms to exploit the architectural characteristics of the target execution platform (CPU, GPU, TPU, or specialized accelerators) to maximize throughput and minimize latency.

It differs from general optimization methods by directly addressing hardware constraints such as cache hierarchy, memory bandwidth, instruction-level parallelism, and execution models, rather than solely optimizing algorithmic complexity or geometric traversal costs.
All methods in this family build on [Ray-grid traversal](17-ray-grid-traversal.md), which advances analytically from one cell boundary to the next .
The core mechanism determines the next cell by comparing distances to upcoming boundaries on the x, y, and z axes, selecting the minimum distance to advance .
Optimization and cost models do not alter this fundamental geometric logic but instead optimize the *cost* of executing it or the *parameters* (like grid resolution) under which it runs.
Hardware-specific optimization in volume rendering has evolved alongside the diversification of computing architectures.
